parameters.description: A 3D point in world space.

parameters.name: normal
parameters.description: A 3D vector in world space. Need not be normalized.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: A 3D vector in world space. Need not be normalized.

function.name: planeSectionPart
function.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, definition is map)
function.description: Split a set of parts with a plane and delete all bodies in front of the face. Unlike sectionPart, bodies which are entirely behind the split plane are retained. Any bodies not included in the target query are deleted.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Bodies to be split.

parameters.name: plane
parameters.description: Plane that splits the bodies. Everything on the positive z side of the plane will be removed.

function.name: planeToCSys
function.description: Create a coordinate system whose XY-plane is a specified plane, with its origin at the plane's origin.

function.name: planeToWorld
function.description: Transforms a 2D point in a Plane's coordinates to its corresponding 3D point in world coordinates.

function.name: planeToWorld3D
function.description: Returns a Transform which takes 3D points measured with respect to a Plane (such that points which lie on the plane will have a z-coordinate of approximately 0) and transforms them into world coordinates.

function.name: pointsManipulator
function.description: A set of points which can be selected one at a time.

parameters.name: points
parameters.description: Array of 3d locations for points

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: The index of the currently selected point

function.name: prepareInitialArcSketch
function.signature: (wrapAroundFront is boolean, modelParameters is map, innerRadius is ValueWithUnits, angle is ValueWithUnits)
function.description: Prepare to sketch the initial arc of the hem or flange, starting at the selected edge and wrapping either around the front of the back of the sheet. Returns information about arc ids and arc end position.

function.name: print
function.description: Print a message to the FeatureScript notices pane.

function.name: println
function.description: Print a message to the FeatureScript notices pane, followed by a newline.

function.name: printTimer
function.description: Prints the elapsed milliseconds for the timer associated with the string timer. Use with startTimer(string).

function.name: processNewBodyIfNeeded
function.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, definition is map, reconstructOp is function)
function.description: This function is designed to be used by body-creating features (like extrude) as a boolean post-processing step with options from booleanStepTypePredicate and booleanStepScopePredicate in the case where the preceding operations of the feature have created new solid or surface bodies. On top of the regular boolean operation, converts the operationType and creates error bodies on failure.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: identifier of the main feature

parameters.name: reconstructOp
parameters.description:
A function which takes in an Id, and reconstructs the input to show to the user as error geometry in case the input is problematic or the boolean itself fails. 
EXAMPLE
function() {} . For a more elaborate example see the source code of revolve feature in the Standard Library.

parameters.name: defaultScope
parameters.description:
OptionalEXAMPLE
true indicates merge scope of "everything else" (default) EXAMPLE
false indicates merge scope is specified in booleanScope

parameters.name: booleanScope
parameters.description: targets to use if defaultScope is false

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: OptionalIf set, will be included in the tools section of the boolean.

parameters.name: mergeScopeExclusion
parameters.description: OptionalIf set, will be excluded from the targets section of the boolean.

function.name: processSubfeatureStatus
function.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, options is map)
function.description: Propagate the status of a subfeature to a feature.

parameters.name: subfeatureId
parameters.description: The Id of the subfeature.

parameters.name: overrideStatus
parameters.description: OptionalA status enum to use instead of the subfeature status enum if the subfeature has an info, warning, or error status.

parameters.name: propagateErrorDisplay
parameters.description: OptionalUse subfeature error display when present. Default is false.

parameters.name: additionalErrorEntities
parameters.description: OptionalAdditional error entities to display if the subfeature has an info, warning, or error status.

function.name: project
function.description: Projects a Line onto a Plane, returning a Line whose origin is on the Plane and whose direction is a normalized Vector on the Plane

function.name: projectCurves
function.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, definition is map)
function.description: Feature creating projected curves.

parameters.name: sketchEdges1
parameters.description: Required if curveProjectionType is TWO_SKETCHES Edges from a single sketch that will be extruded to perform an intersection.

parameters.name: sketchEdges2
parameters.description: Required if curveProjectionType is TWO_SKETCHES Edges from a single sketch that will be extruded to perform an intersection.

parameters.name: dropTools
parameters.description: Required if curveProjectionType is CURVE_TO_FACE Edges that will be projected onto targets.

parameters.name: directionQuery
parameters.description: Required if projectionType is DIRECTION Specifies the direction of projection.

parameters.name: oppositeDirection
parameters.description: Required if projectionType is DIRECTION If true, negates the direction supplied by directionQuery.

parameters.name: targets
parameters.description: Required if curveProjectionType is CURVE_TO_FACE Faces, sheet bodies, or solid bodies to project onto.

function.name: qActiveSheetMetalFilter
function.description: A query for all entities in queryToFilter belonging to an active sheet metal part.

function.name: qAdjacent
function.signature: (seed is Query, adjacencyType is AdjacencyType, entityType is EntityType)
function.description: A query for entities that are adjacent to the given seed entities.

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: One or more entities whose adjacent neighbors are queried. The result does not include the original seed entities (unless they are adjacent to other seed entities)

function.name: qAllModifiableSolidBodies
function.description: A query for all modifiable solid bodies, including mesh-containing bodies.

function.name: qAllModifiableSolidBodiesNoMesh
function.description: A query for all solid bodies that do not have mesh geometry or in context geometry, i.e. every non-mesh-containing part displayed in the Part Studio's "Parts" list.

function.name: qAllNonMeshSolidBodies
function.description: A query for all solid bodies that do not have mesh geometry.

function.name: qAllSolidBodies
function.description: A query for all solid bodies.

function.name: qAttributeFilter
function.description: Note: This query is used only for legacy unnamed attributes, which are still supported but no longer reccommended. See the Attributes module for details.

parameters.name: attributePattern
parameters.description:
Will only resolve to queries whose legacy unnamed attributes match the type (and possibly the values) of this pattern.
If attributePattern has a type tag, will only match attributes with that same type tag. 
EXAMPLE
{} as MyCustomType will match all attributes with type tag MyCustomTypeIf the attribute has no type tag (i.e. it is a standard type like string or map), will match all attributes with that same standard type. 
EXAMPLE
"asdf" will match all string attributes. EXAMPLE
{} will match all map attributes.If the attribute is a map, will only match maps which have identical values for every key-value pair in the pattern 
EXAMPLE
{ "odd" : true } matches all unnamed map attributes that have a field "odd" whose value is true. EXAMPLE
{ "odd" : true } as MyCustomType matches all unnamed map attributes with the that have a field "odd" whose value is true.

function.name: qAttributeQuery
function.description: Note: This query is used only for legacy unnamed attributes, which are still supported but no longer reccommended. See the Attributes module for details.

function.name: qAxis
function.description: A query that filters edges and faces into axis-symmetric ones (lines, circles, cylinders, cones, tori, revolved, mate connectors) that have the given axis. The sign of the axis direction does not matter.

function.name: qBodiesWithFormAttribute
function.description: Query for all bodies in queryToFilter marked with a FormAttribute and value exactly equal to attribute

function.name: qBodiesWithFormAttributes
function.description: Query for all bodies in queryToFilter marked with a FormAttribute and value exactly equal to one of the attributes

function.name: qBodyType
function.description: A query for all entities in queryToFilter which are bodies of the a specified BodyType, or are owned by bodies with the specified BodyType

function.name: qCapEntity
function.signature: (featureId is Id, capType is CapType, entityType is EntityType)
function.description: A query for start/end cap vertex, edge, and face entities created by featureId. Cap entities are produced by extrude, revolve, sweep, loft and thicken features

function.name: qClosestTo
function.description: A query for the entity in queryToFilter closest to a point.

parameters.name: point
parameters.description: A position vector for the point to find entities closest to.

function.name: qCoincidesWithPlane
function.description: A query for all entities (bodies, faces, edges, or points) in queryToFilter coinciding with a specified infinite plane.

parameters.name: plane
parameters.description:
EXAMPLE
plane(vector(0, 0, 0) * meter, vector(0, 0, 1))

function.name: qCompositePartsContaining
function.description: A query for each composite part of the given type containing bodies.

function.name: qCompositePartTypeFilter
function.description: A query for all bodies in queryToFilter which are either open or closed composite parts, depending on the second parameter.

function.name: qConcaveConnectedFaces
function.description: A query for a set of faces connected to seed via concave edges, flood-filling across any number of concave edges.

function.name: qConstructionFilter
function.description: A query for all construction entities or all non-construction entities in queryToFilter.

function.name: qConsumed
function.description: A query for all entities in queryToFilter which are consumed by any closed composite part, or all entities of queryToFilter which are not consumed by any closed composite part.

function.name: qContainedInCompositeParts
function.description: A query for each part contained in compositeParts.

function.name: qContainsPoint
function.description: A query for all entities (bodies, faces, edges, or points) in queryToFilter containing a specified point.

parameters.name: point
parameters.description: A 3D point, in world space.

function.name: qConvexConnectedFaces
function.description: A query for a set of faces connected to seed via convex edges, flood-filling across any number of convex edges.

function.name: qCorrespondingInFlat
function.description: A query for entities in sheet metal flattened body corresponding to any entitiesInFolded which are part of 3D sheet metal bodies

function.name: qCreatedBy
function.description: A query for all the entities created by a feature or operation. The feature is given by its feature id, which was passed into the the operation function in order to create the feature.

parameters.name: featureId
parameters.description:
The Id of the specified feature. 
EXAMPLE
id + "extrude1"

function.name: qDefaultBodies
function.description: A query for all default created bodies in a context, that is, the top, right, front planes and the origin point.

function.name: qDependency
function.description: A query for the true dependency of the given dependentEntities. For instance, the true dependency of the extruded body will be the face or sketch edges of the profile from which it is extruded.

function.name: qEdgeAdjacent
function.description: Deprecated: Use qAdjacent with AdjacencyType.EDGE

function.name: qEdgeConvexityTypeFilter
function.description: A query that filters given edges by convexity.

function.name: qEdgeTopologyFilter
function.description: A query for edges in a queryToFilter which match a given EdgeTopology.

function.name: qEdgeVertex
function.description: A query for the start or end vertices of edges.

function.name: qEntityFilter
function.description: A query for entities in a queryToFilter which match a given EntityType.

function.name: qEverything
function.description: A query for all entities of a specified EntityType in the context.

function.name: qFaceOrEdgeBoundedFaces
function.description: Given a seed face and bounding entities, matches all adjacent faces inside the bounding entities, expanding from the seed face.

parameters.name: faceAndBoundingEntities
parameters.description: A Query for the seed face, followed by any boundary faces or edges. The seed face must be first, so a qUnion should be used to guarantee the order.

function.name: qFacesParallelToDirection
function.description: A query for all faces in queryToFilter that are parallel to the given direction vector e.g. if it is a planar face, the plane normal is perpendicular to direction if it is a cylindrical face, the axis is parallel to direction if it is an extruded face, the extrude direction is parallel to direction

function.name: qFarthestAlong
function.description: A query for the entity in queryToFilter farthest along a direction in world space. In the case of a tie, resolves to all entities within TOLERANCE.zeroLength of being the farthest.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: A vector for the direction to find the entity farthest away.

function.name: qFilletFaces
function.description: A query for fillet faces of radius equal to, less than or equal to, or greater than or equal to the input faces. If facesToCompareTo does not match one or more fillet faces, the resulting query will not match any faces. Will find the fillet radius from each face and compare to find faces of all fillets on that body that satisfy the compareType.

function.name: qFlattenedCompositeParts
function.description: A query for non-composite entities in entities and constituents of composite parts in entities.

function.name: qFrontPlane
function.description: A query for the front plane.

function.name: qGeometry
function.description: A query for all entities in queryToFilter with a specified GeometryType.

function.name: qHasAttribute
function.description: Query for all entities in queryToFilter marked with an attribute with name name

function.name: qHasAttributeWithValue
function.signature: (queryToFilter is Query, name is string, value)
function.description: Query for all entities in queryToFilter marked with an attribute with name name and value exactly equal to value

function.name: qHasAttributeWithValueMatching
function.signature: (queryToFilter is Query, name is string, attributePattern is map)
function.description: Query for all entities in queryToFilter marked with an attribute with name name and a map value matching every key-value pair in the provided attributePattern map.

parameters.name: attributePattern

function.name: qHoleFaces
function.description: Given a single face inside a hole or hole-like geometry, returns all faces of that hole.

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: A query for a single face inside the hole.

function.name: qInFrontOfPlane
function.description: A query for all entities (bodies, faces, edges, or points) in queryToFilter in front of a specified infinite plane. Entities intersecting the plane will not be resolved. Only entities completely on one side or coincident with the plane will be selected. Use flip(plane) to query entities on the other side of the plane. For example, for the XY plane through the origin with the normal (0, 0, 1), qInFrontOfPlane will resolve the vertices (1, 1, 0) and (1, 1, 1) but not the vertex (1, 1, -1).

parameters.name: plane
parameters.description:
EXAMPLE
plane(vector(0, 0, 0) * meter, vector(0, 0, 1))

function.name: qIntersectsLine
function.description: A query for all entities (bodies, faces, edges, or points) in queryToFilter touching a specified infinite line.

function.name: qIntersectsPlane
function.description: A query for all entities (bodies, faces, edges, or points) in queryToFilter touching a specified infinite plane.

parameters.name: plane
parameters.description:
EXAMPLE
plane(vector(0, 0, 0) * meter, vector(0, 0, 1))

function.name: qLaminarDependency
function.description: A query for the true dependency of the given dependentEntities, specifically for use with wire edges that have been created from laminar edges. If the immediate dependency is not laminar then it will track back until it reaches a laminar dependency (if there is one).

function.name: qLargest
function.description: A query to find the largest entity (by length, area, or volume) in queryToFilter.

function.name: qLoopBoundedFaces
function.description: Given a face and an edge, query for all faces bounded by the given face, on the side of the given edge.

parameters.name: faceAndEdge
parameters.description: Should match a face and an edge. If multiple faces and edges match, used the first face and the first edge.

function.name: qLoopEdges
function.description: A query for a set of edges defining a loop. If the seed has laminar edges, this query will extend to include all laminar loops that contain any seed edges. If the seed has faces, the result will include the loops forming the outer boundary of the joined faces.

function.name: qMatching
function.description: Matches any faces or edges within owner bodies of entities in referenceEntities which are geometrically identical (same size and shape) to the face or edge in referenceEntities.

function.name: qMateConnectorsOfParts
function.description: A query for all mate connectors owned by parts.

function.name: qMeshGeometryFilter
function.description: A query for all mesh entities or all non-mesh entities in queryToFilter.

function.name: qModifiableEntityFilter
function.description: A query for all modifiable entities in queryToFilter.

function.name: qNonCapEntity
function.description: A query for vertex, edge, and face entities created by featureId that are not cap entities. Cap entities are produced by extrude, revolve, sweep, loft and thicken features

function.name: qNothing
function.description: An empty query, which does not resolve to any entities.

function.name: qNthElement
function.description: A query for one entity in queryToFilter at a specified index. The order of entities resolved by a query is deterministic but arbitrary.

parameters.name: queryToFilter
parameters.description: A query which resolves to at least n+1 entities

parameters.name: n
parameters.description:
Zero-based index of entity in queryToFilter. 
EXAMPLE
0 indicates the first entity EXAMPLE
-1 indicates the last entity

function.name: qOpHoleFace
function.description: A query for the hole faces created by an opHole operation.

parameters.name: featureId
parameters.description:
The Id of the specified operation. 
EXAMPLE
id + "hole1"

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: OptionalFilter the query for faces with a given name. See faceNames field of HoleDefinition.

parameters.name: identity
parameters.description: OptionalFilter the query for the hole associated with the given identity entity. See identities parameter of opHole.

function.name: qOpHoleProfile
function.description: A query for the profile edges or vertices created by an opHole operation.

parameters.name: featureId
parameters.description:
The Id of the specified operation. 
EXAMPLE
id + "hole1"

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: OptionalFilter the query for profiles with a given name. See name field of HoleProfile.

parameters.name: identity
parameters.description: OptionalFilter the query for the hole associated with the given identity entity. See identities parameter of opHole.

function.name: qOrigin
function.description: A query for the origin point.

function.name: qOwnedByBody
function.description: A query for all of the entities (faces, vertices, edges, and bodies) in a context which belong to a specified body or bodies.

function.name: qOwnerBody
function.description: A query for each body that any of the given entities belong to.

function.name: qParallelEdges
function.description: A query to find all linear edges in queryToFilter which are parallel (or anti-parallel) to any linear edge in edges.

function.name: qParallelPlanes
function.signature: (queryToFilter is Query, normal is Vector, allowAntiparallel is boolean)
function.description: A query for all planar face entities in queryToFilter that are parallel to a plane specified by the normal vector.

parameters.name: normal
parameters.description: The normal vector to reference when checking for parallelism.

parameters.name: allowAntiparallel
parameters.description: Whether to also return entities that are antiparallel.

function.name: qPartsAttachedTo
function.description: A query for parts to which sheetMetalEntities are attached (e.g. sheet metal bend line entities are attached to a flattened sheet metal part)

function.name: qPatternInstances
function.signature: (featureId is Id, instanceNames is array, entityType is EntityType)
function.description: A query for entities created by a specific instance or instances of an opPattern operation.

parameters.name: featureId
parameters.description:
The Id of the specified feature. 
EXAMPLE
id + "pattern1"

parameters.name: instanceNames
parameters.description: The names of the instances to query for, a subset of the instanceNames passed into the opPattern operation.

function.name: qPlanesParallelToDirection
function.description: A query for all planar faces in queryToFilter that are parallel to the given direction vector (i.e., the plane normal is perpendicular to direction).

function.name: qRightPlane
function.description: A query for the right plane.

function.name: qSheetMetalFlatFilter
function.description: A query for all entities in queryToFilter belonging to a flattened sheet metal part.

function.name: qSheetMetalFormFilter
function.description: A query for all entities in queryToFilter that are artifacts of a sheet metal form feature on flat pattern.

function.name: qSketchFilter
function.description: A query for all sketch entities, or all non-sketch entities in queryToFilter.

function.name: qSketchRegion
function.description: A query for all fully enclosed, 2D regions created by a sketch.

parameters.name: featureId
parameters.description: The feature id of the Sketch being queried.

parameters.name: filterInnerLoops
parameters.description: OptionalSpecifies whether to exclude sketch regions fully contained in other sketch regions. A region whose border has a vertex or edge on the outside boundary is not considered "contained." Default is false.

function.name: qSmallest
function.description: A query to find the smallest entity (by length, area, or volume) in queryToFilter.

function.name: qSMDefinitionEntityFilter
function.description: A query for sheet metal definition entities in a queryToFilter which match a given EntityType.

function.name: qSMFlatFilter
function.description: Deprecated: Use qSheetMetalFlatFilter

function.name: qSourceMesh
function.description: A query for each mesh element that any selectedMeshVertices belong to. selectedMeshVertices should be the point bodies created when a user selects a mesh vertex. Mesh vertices which have not been selected cannot be queried in FeatureScript

parameters.name: selectedMeshVertices
parameters.description: One or more mesh vertices whose owning elements are queried.

function.name: qSplitBy
function.signature: (featureId is Id, entityType, backBody is boolean)
function.description: Given the id of a split feature, get entities of a given EntityType on the front or the back side of the split. For a split by face or part, the front denotes the body in the direction of the split tool's surface normal, and the back denotes the body opposite the normal. For a split by isocline, the front denotes non-steep faces and edges, and the back denotes steep entities.

parameters.name: featureId
parameters.description:
EXAMPLE
id + "split1"

parameters.name: backBody
parameters.description:
EXAMPLE
false indicates the entities in the front. EXAMPLE
true indicates the entities in the back.

function.name: qSubtraction
function.description: A query for entities which match query1, but do not match query2. qSubtraction preserves the order of query1.

function.name: qSymmetricDifference
function.description: A query for entities which match either query1 or query2, but not both.

function.name: qTangentConnectedEdges
function.description: A query for a chain of tangent edges connected to seed via tangent vertices, chaining across any number of tangent vertices.

function.name: qTangentConnectedFaces
function.description: A query for a set of faces connected to seed via tangent edges, flood-filling across any number of tangent edges.

function.name: qTopPlane
function.description: A query for the top plane.

function.name: queryVariable
function.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, definition is map)
function.description: Feature to create a query variable via calling setQueryVariable. This variable may be used in featurescript via call getQueryVariable or in the UI by clicking the "Variable selection" dropdown in the feature dialog or by selecting the query variable feature in the feature list.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the feature. Must not belong to a non-query variable feature. If a query variable feature with this name exists, it will be overwritten after this feature.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Description of the variable. Maximum length of 256 characters.

parameters.name: selectionQuery
parameters.description: If selectionType is SELECTION, query that will be contained in the variable.

parameters.name: createdByFeatures
parameters.description: If selectionType is CREATED_BY, features whose created entities will be contained in the variable.

parameters.name: seedBodies
parameters.description: If selectionType is OWNED_BY or EDGE_CONVEXITY, bodies owning the entities that will be contained in the variable.

parameters.name: seedFaces
parameters.description: If selectionType is PROTRUSION or POCKET or HOLE or FILLETS or BOUNDED_FACES, or TANGENT_CONNECTED or MATCHING and seedType is FACE, faces from which the selection is created.

parameters.name: seedEdgesOrFaces
parameters.description: If selectionType is LOOP_CHAIN_CONNECTED, faces or edges from which the loops are computed.

parameters.name: boundedFacesBounds
parameters.description: If selectionType is BOUNDED_FACES, the faces or edges bounding the selection.

parameters.name: addAdditionalQueries
parameters.description: Whether to include addition queries in the variable.

parameters.name: additionalQueries
parameters.description: An array of additional queries to include. Each item's content is analogous to what is contained in the original query. It also contains a booleanOperation field determining how to combine the additional query with the current query.

parameters.name: evaluateOnUse
parameters.description: Whether to evaluate the variable when it is created or when it is used.

parameters.name: showSelection
parameters.description: Whether to highlight the entities contained in the created variable.

function.name: qUnion
function.signature: (query1 is Query, query2 is Query, query3 is Query, query4 is Query)

function.name: qUniqueVertices
function.description: A query that filters out duplicate vertices. When duplicates are found, the vertex with the lowest deterministic ID is used.

function.name: qVertexAdjacent
function.description: Deprecated: Use qAdjacent with AdjacencyType.VERTEX

function.name: qWithinRadius
function.signature: (queryToFilter is Query, point is Vector, radius is ValueWithUnits)
function.description: A query for all entities (bodies, faces, edges or points) in queryToFilter that are within a specified radius from a point.

parameters.name: point
parameters.description: The point from which to check distance from.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: The distance away from the point.

function.name: range
function.description: Return an array of numbers, (of type number or ValueWithUnits), in a range. Note: before FeatureScript 372 this function received as input the step size instead of the number of steps

function.name: reciprocal
function.description: Inverts a value, including units.

function.name: regenError
function.signature: (customMessage is string, faultyParameters is array, entities is Query)
function.description: An array of strings that correspond to keys in the feature definition map. Throwing a regenError with faultyParameters will highlight them in red inside the feature dialog.

parameters.name: entities
parameters.description: A query for entities to highlight in the Part Studio. Multiple queries can be combined and highlighted using the qUnion function. The entities are only highlighted when the feature dialog is open.

function.name: remapCornerBreaks
function.description: Remap corner breaks on walls whose wall id has changed. Takes the output of collectCornerBreakTracking as cornerBreakTracking.

function.name: removeAttributes
function.description: Has no effect on named attributes, instead use setAttribute with "attribute" : undefined.

parameters.name: entities
parameters.description: OptionalEntities to remove unnamed attributes from. Default is everything.

parameters.name: attributePattern
parameters.description: OptionalIf provided, will only remove attributes with the same type, using the same behavior documented in the legacy function qAttributeFilter.

function.name: removeElementAt
function.description: Returns an array with the element at index removed.

function.name: removeKnots
function.signature: (points is array, knots is array, curveDegree is number)
function.description: Remove as many knots as possible from a NURBS defined by points, knots and curveDegree.

function.name: repeatString
function.description: Return a string made by repeating the first argument a specified number of times. For example: repeatString("foo", 5) returns "foofoofoofoofoo".

function.name: replace
function.signature: (s is string, regExp is string, replacement is string)
function.description: Returns a copy of s with every match of regExp replaced with the string replacement.

function.name: replaceFace
function.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, definition is map)
function.description: Feature performing an opReplaceFace.

function.name: replaceSMAttribute
function.signature: (context is Context, existingAttribute is SMAttribute, newAttribute is SMAttribute)
function.description: For all entities annotated with attribute matching existingAttribute pattern, replace it with newAttribute. Return query for entities whose attributes have been modified.

function.name: reportFeatureInfo
function.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, message is ErrorStringEnum, associatedParameters is array)
function.description: Attaches an info-level status to the given feature id. Will display a notification to the user containing the specified message.

function.name: reportFeatureStatus
function.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, status is FeatureStatus)
function.description: Report the status of a feature

function.name: reportFeatureWarning
function.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, message is ErrorStringEnum, associatedParameters is array)
function.description: Attaches custom warning-level status to the given feature id. Will display a notification to the user containing the specified message.

function.name: resize
function.signature: (arr is array, newSize is number, newValue)
function.description: Returns a copy of an array with size changed to newSize. If the new size is larger than the original size, the extra values are set to newValue.

function.name: reverse
function.description: Return a copy of an array with elements in reverse order.

function.name: setDimensionedEntities
function.description: Tolerant dimensions require multiple pieces of information. This function specifies all of the information required for a dimension that cannot be specified in a tolerant quantity. Tolerant quantities are commonly declared in a feature using the UIHint.CAN_BE_TOLERANT or UIHint.CAN_BE_TOLERANT_DIAMETER UI hints in the annotation of the quantity parameter.

parameters.name: parameterId
parameters.description: The id of the tolerant quantity parameter in the feature definition.

parameters.name: queries
parameters.description: An array of one query (for a radius or diameter dimension) or two queries (for other dimensions). The queries can evaluate to more than one face, but in that case each face should lie on the same underlying surface. See extrude and fillet for examples.

parameters.name: facePairs
parameters.description: Required if queries is undefinedAn array of pairs of queries (a pair is an array of two queries). Used for features where mulitple face pairs are subject to the same constraint but they are not all coincident, for example, a thin extrusion of a square where the thickness is tolerant.

parameters.name: measuresSolidAngle
parameters.description: OptionalUsed to specify which part of a circle an angle dimension refers to. The angle between two planes can be defined by two possible numbers that sum to 360 degrees. If this option is SOLID, then the angle is measured from the first face, in to the part. If this option is VOID, then the angle is measured from the first face, out of the part. If this option is not set for an angle, then the result is consistent but undefined. It is recommended that an option is always provided for angle dimensions.

parameters.name: measurementDirection
parameters.description: OptionalUsed with dimensions of type FeatureDimensionType.AXIS_DISTANCE. If this option is not set then the dimension measures the shortest distance between the axes. If this option is set then the dimension measures the distance between the axes in this direction.

parameters.name: schemaClass
parameters.description: OptionalOn regeneration a dimension with a quantity with tolerance type ToleranceType.DEFAULT will set its tolerances given the nominal value and any default tolerances specified on the part. If this field is not set then the rule used will be either the default linear or angular rule, depending on the dimension type. If this field is set then the dimension will use the custom rule corresponding to the value. This field can also be a ToleranceSchemaClass to use a predefined class from the standard library. For example, you can set this to ToleranceSchemaClass.FILLET_RADIUS to use the same tolerance rules as Onshape's official fillet feature.

parameters.name: tolerances
parameters.description: OptionalContains tolerance and precision information for the specified parameter. This cannot be set if the parameter has been marked tolerant by the user.

parameters.name: nominal
parameters.description: Required if tolerances is not undefinedRequired if setting tolerances, for either an existing or new parameter. For an existing feature parameter, this is usually the value of that parameter.

enum.name: HolePositionReference
enum.description: For a HoleProfile, a reference point along the hole axis to which the position of the profile is relative. To calculate these references, the cylinder of the hole is intersected with the targets of the hole. If the hole cylinder encounters a slanted or otherwise irregular face at the intersection with the target, the reference may by a range rather than a single point. Users may specify that they want the end of this range by using a holeProfile, or the beginning of this range by using a holeProfileBeforeReference; or they may control this behavior directly by setting the beforeReference flag of the HoleProfile.

parameters.name: AXIS_POINT
parameters.type: When calling opHole, the user will supply one or more axes defining where the holes are to be placed. When using this reference, the position of the profile will be in reference to the origin of the axis Line of the hole.

parameters.name: TARGET_START
parameters.type: When using this reference, the position of the profile will be in reference to the closest intersection of the hole cylinder with any target.

parameters.name: LAST_TARGET_START
parameters.type: For each target, find the first intersection of the hole cylinder into the target. When using this reference, the position of the profile will be in reference to the furthest of those intersections. Notably, this means that if certain targets are geometrically constructed such that the hole cylinder enters and exits the target multiple times, only the first of the entrances into the target is considered.

parameters.name: LAST_TARGET_END
parameters.type: When using this reference, the position of the profile will be in reference to the furthest exit of the hole cylinder from any target.

parameters.name: LAST_TARGET_START_IN_DEPTH
parameters.type: For each target, find the first intersection of the hole cylinder into the target. When using this reference, the position of the profile will be in reference to the furthest of those intersections within the hole depth.

Modeling.name: DistanceResult
Modeling.description: The result of an evDistance call -- information about the extremal distance and the attaining point / line / entity.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: Description

parameters.name: distance
parameters.description: The minimal or maximal distance.

parameters.name: sides
parameters.description:
An array of 2 maps, containing information about where the extremum was found for each side. Each map has a:
point (Vector) : The position in world space that is closest or farthest to the other side. The distance field is measured between the two values of point.
index (integer) : the index into the line or point array or into the query results, if a query is passed in.
parameter (number or length or array of two numbers) : If the index refers to an edge, the parameter is a number between 0 and 1 (unless extend for that side was passed in). It is in the form that evEdgeTangentLine and evEdgeCurvature consume (with arcLengthParameterization set to the same value that was passed into evDistance).
If the index refers to a point, the parameter is 0.
If the index refers to a Line, the parameter is a length representing the distance along the direction.
If the index refers to a face, the parameter is a 2D Vector in the form that evFaceTangentPlane consumes. If this face is a mesh or a plane, the parameter is a 2D Vector of zeroes.
If the index refers to a Plane, the parameter is a 2D Vector representing the lengths along the plane's x and y axes.

Modeling.name: evaluateQuery
Modeling.description: Returns an array of queries for the individual entities in a context which match a specified query. The returned array contains exactly one transient query for each matching entity at the time of the call. If the context is modified, the returned queries may become invalid and no longer match an entity.

Modeling.name: evaluateQueryCount
Modeling.description: Returns the number of entities returned by the supplied query. Equivalent to size(evaluateQuery(context, query)), but faster.

Modeling.name: evApproximateBSplineCurve
Modeling.description: Given a query for a curve, return its approximation (or exact representation if possible) as a B-spline. The options forceCubic and forceNonRational may be used to restrict the type of spline that is returned, but even if these options are false, a cubic non-rational spline may be returned.

parameters.name: edge
parameters.description: The curve to approximate.

parameters.name: forceCubic
parameters.description: OptionalIf true, a cubic spline will be returned. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: forceNonRational
parameters.description: OptionalIf true, a non-rational spline will be returned. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: tolerance
parameters.description: OptionalSpecifies the desired approximation tolerance: the maximum distance (in meters) between the original curve and the returned spline representation. Default is 1e-6, minimum is 1e-8, and maximum is 1e-2.

Modeling.name: evApproximateBSplineSurface
Modeling.description: Given a query for a face, return its approximation as a B-spline, including trim boundaries. The options forceCubic and forceNonRational may be used to restrict the type of spline that is returned for the surface, but even if these options are false, a cubic non-rational spline may be returned.

parameters.name: face
parameters.description: The curve to approximate.

parameters.name: forceCubic
parameters.description: OptionalIf true, the returned surface will be a cubic spline. This does not affect the trim curves. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: forceNonRational
parameters.description: OptionalIf true, the returned surface will be non-rational. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: tolerance
parameters.description: OptionalSpecifies the desired approximation tolerance: the maximum distance (in meters) between the original face and the returned spline representation. Default is 1e-6, minimum is 1e-8, and maximum is 1e-4. The tolerance for trim curves is 10x the specified value.

parameters.name: Return
parameters.description: Description

parameters.name: bSplineSurface
parameters.description: the underlying 3D surface

parameters.name: boundaryBSplineCurves
parameters.description: array of 2D BSplineCurves representing the trimming boundary of the face. May be empty if the face is the entirety of the surface.

parameters.name: innerLoopBSplineCurves
parameters.description: array of arrays of 2D BSplineCurves representing the inner loops (if any) of the trimming boundary of the face.

Modeling.name: evApproximateCentroid
Modeling.description: Find the centroid of an entity or group of entities. This is equivalent to the center of mass for a constant density object. Warning: This is an approximate value and it is not recommended to use this for modeling purposes that will be negatively affected in case the approximation changes. Consider using the center of a bounding box instead.

parameters.name: entities
parameters.description: The entities to take the center of mass of.

Modeling.name: evApproximateMassProperties
Modeling.description: Calculates approximate mass properties of an entity or group of entities. Returns mass, centroid, inertia tensor, and volume/area/length/count for bodies/faces/edges/vertices, respectively. Warning: These are approximate values and it is not recommended to use them for modeling purposes that will be negatively affected in case the approximation changes.

parameters.name: entities
parameters.description: The entities of which to compute mass properties. Only entities of the highest dimensionality will be considered.

parameters.name: density
parameters.description:
The density of the entities, with appropriate units. 
EXAMPLE
1 * kilogram / meter ^ 3 could be the density of 3D solid bodies EXAMPLE
1 * kilogram / meter ^ 2 could be the density of 2D faces or sheet bodies EXAMPLE
1 * kilogram / meter could be the density of 1D edges or wire bodies EXAMPLE
1 * kilogram could be the mass of each 0D vertex or point body

parameters.name: referenceFrame
parameters.description: OptionalOptional coordinate system. Defaults to the centroid with world axes for the inertia tensor, and world coordinates for the centroid.

Modeling.name: evArea
Modeling.description: Return the total area of all the entities. If no matching 2D faces are found the total area will be zero.

Modeling.name: evAxis
Modeling.description: If the query finds one entity with an axis -- a line, circle, cylinder, cone, sphere, torus, mate connector, or revolved surface -- return the axis. Otherwise throw an exception.

Modeling.name: evDistance

One of the following: A query, or a point (3D Length Vector), or a Line, or a Plane, or an array of points, or an array of Lines, or an array of Planes. 
EXAMPLE
qNthElement(qEverything(EntityType.FACE), 0) or vector(1, 2, 3) * meter or line(vector(1, 0, 1) * meter, vector(1, 1, 1) or plane(vector(1,1,1) * meter, vector(0,0,1), vector(1,0,0)).

Modeling.name: opBoundarySurface
Modeling.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, definition is map)
Modeling.description: Creates a boundary surface fitting two ordered sets of profiles.

parameters.name: uProfileSubqueries
parameters.description:
An ordered array of two or fewer queries for the profiles in the u direction. These can be edges or wire bodies. 
EXAMPLE
[ profileQuery1, profileQuery2 ]

parameters.name: vProfileSubqueries
parameters.description:
OptionalAn ordered array of two or fewer queries for the profiles in the v direction. These can be edges or wire bodies. 
EXAMPLE
[ profileQuery1, profileQuery2 ]

parameters.name: uDerivativeInfo
parameters.description:
OptionalAn array of maps that contain shape constraints at start and end profiles. Each map entry is required to have a profileIndex that refers to the affected profile. Optional fields include a vector to match surface tangent to, a magnitude, and booleans for matching tangents or curvature derived from faces adjacent to affected profile. 
EXAMPLE
[ { "profileIndex" : 0, "vector" : vector(1, 0, 0), "magnitude" : 2., "tangentToPlane" : true}, { "profileIndex" : 1, "adjacentFaces" : qFaces } ] The first map would constrain the resulting boundary surface at the first u profile to be tangent to plane with normal vector(1,0,0) and magnitude 2. The second map constrains the boundary surface at the second u profile to match tangents of faces defined by the query qFaces.

parameters.name: vDerivativeInfo
parameters.description: OptionalAn array of maps analogous to uDerivativeInfo, but for v profiles.

parameters.name: showIsocurves
parameters.description: OptionalShow graphical representation of a subset of isoparameteric curves on each face of the created boundary surface. Default false.

parameters.name: curveCount

Modeling.name: opCreateIsocline
Modeling.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, definition is map)
Modeling.description: Creates wires corresponding to the given faces's isocline edges. Each isocline follows a path along a face with a constant angle in the (-90, 90) degree range (e.g., lines of latitude on a sphere). This angle is the face tangent plane's angle with respect to the direction with its sign determined by the dot product of direction and the face normal, and is analogous to the angle used in draft analysis. Depending on the face geometry, there may be zero, one, or multiple isoclines on each face.

parameters.name: faces
parameters.description: The faces on which to imprint isoclines.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: A reference direction.

parameters.name: angle
parameters.description: The isocline angle with respect to the direction in the (-90, 90) degree range.

parameters.description: OptionalAn array of queries for guide curves. Each guide curve should intersect each profile once.

parameters.description:
OptionalAn array of maps to define multiple profile alignments. Each connection map should contain:
(1) connectionEntities query describing an array of vertices or edges (one per profile),
(2) connectionEdges an array of individual queries for edges in connectionEntities. The order of individual edge queries should be synchronized with connectionEdgeParameters.
(3) connectionEdgeParameters array - an ordered and synchronized array of parameters on edges in connectionEdgeQueries 
EXAMPLE
[ {"connectionEntities" : qVertexAndEdge1, "connectionEdges" : [qEdge1], "connectionEdgeParameters" : [0.25]} {"connectionEntities" : qVertexAndEdge2, "connectionEdges" : [qEdge2], "connectionEdgeParameters" : [0.75]}]

Optional fields include a vector to match surface tangent to, a magnitude, and booleans for matching tangents or curvature derived from faces adjacent to affected profile. 
EXAMPLE
[ { "profileIndex" : 0, "vector" : vector(1, 0, 0), "magnitude" : 2., "tangentToPlane" : true}, { "profileIndex" : 1, "matchCurvature" : true, "adjacentFaces" : qFaces } ] The first map would constrain the resulting loft at the start profile to be tangent to plane with normal vector(1,0,0) and magnitude 2. Modeling.name: opSplitByIsocline
Modeling.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, definition is map)
Modeling.description: Split the given faces by isocline edges. Each isocline follows a path along a face with a constant angle in the (-90, 90) degree range (e.g., lines of latitude on a sphere). This angle is the face tangent plane's angle with respect to the direction with its sign determined by the dot product of direction and the face normal, and is analogous to the angle used in draft analysis. Depending on the face geometry, there may be zero, one, or multiple isoclines on each face. The isocline edges are created as new edges which split the provided faces. The resulting faces are either steep (i.e., the angle is less than the input angle) or non-steep. To instead leave the original faces intact, you can first extract the faces with opExtractSurface(), and create isoclines on the resulting surfaces. The isocline edges can be queried for with qCreatedBy. The split orientation is consistent such that the non-steep faces are always in "front" of the split, and can be reliably queried for with qSplitBy:

parameters.name: faces
parameters.description: The faces on which to imprint isoclines.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: A reference direction.

parameters.name: angle
parameters.description: The isocline angle with respect to the direction in the (-90, 90) degree range.

The shadow curve edges are created as new edges which split the faces of the provided bodies. Each of the resulting faces is wholly visible or wholly invisible. Edge-on faces are considered invisible. The shadow curve edges can be queried for with qCreatedBy. The split orientation is consistent such that the visible faces are always in "front" of the split, and can be reliably queried for with qSplitBy:

(1) connectionEntities query describing an array of vertices or edges (one per profile),
(2) connectionEdges an array of individual queries for edges in connectionEntities. The order of individual edge queries should be synchronized with connectionEdgeParameters.
(3) connectionEdgeParameters array - an ordered and synchronized array of parameters on edges in connectionEdgeQueries

Modeling.name: opThicken
Modeling.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, definition is map)
Modeling.description: Thicken sheet bodies and faces into solid bodies.

parameters.name: entities
parameters.description: The sheet bodies and faces to thicken.

parameters.name: thickness2
parameters.description: The distance by which to thicken in the opposite direction.

parameters.name: keepTools
parameters.description: OptionalDefault is true. If false the operation will attempt to delete the entities. The operation will not delete sheet bodies unless the sheet body or all faces of the sheet body are selected. The operation will not delete sketches or solid bodies.

Modeling.name: opTransform
Modeling.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, definition is map)
Modeling.description: Applies a given transform to one or more bodies. To make transformed copies of bodies, use opPattern.

parameters.name: bodies
parameters.description: The bodies to transform.

parameters.name: transform
parameters.description:
The transform to apply. 
EXAMPLE
transform(vector(0, 0, 1) * inch) will translate the body 1 inch along the world's z-axis. EXAMPLE
rotationAround(myLine, 30 * degree) will rotate around a Line object. EXAMPLE
scaleUniformly(factor) will scale uniformly about the origin. EXAMPLE
scaleUniformly(factor, point) will scale uniformly about a given point. EXAMPLE
toWorld(cSys) will (somewhat counterintuitively) perform a transform such that geometry on the world's origin and axes will move to the cSys origin and axes. EXAMPLE
fromWorld(cSys) will (somewhat counterintuitively) perform a transform such that geometry on the cSys origin and axes will move to the world origin and axes. EXAMPLE
transform2 * transform1 will perform transform1, followed by transform2.

Modeling.name: opWrap
Modeling.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, definition is map)
Modeling.description: Wraps or unwraps faces from one surface onto another. The location and orientation of the wrapped faces on the destination surface are controlled by the anchorPoint and anchorDirection of the source and destination WrapSurfaces. The entities of the operation are not affected, the result of this operation is a new set of surface bodies or imprinted edges representing the wrapped or unwrapped faces. Faces that are topologically connected will remain topologically connected in the result body for WrapType.SIMPLE and WrapType.TRIM. This operation currently supports wrapping from a plane onto a cylinder or a cone, and unwrapping from a cylinder or a cone onto a plane.

parameters.name: entities
parameters.description: Faces to wrap from source to destination.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: The surface to wrap from. All entities must lie on this surface.

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description: The surface to wrap onto. Must be defined using the face field for WrapType.TRIM or WrapType.IMPRINT.

parameters.name: orientWithDestination
parameters.description: OptionalIf true (default), the normals of the resulting surface will point in the same direction as the destination. If false, the normals of the resulting surface will point in the opposite direction. For the purpose of this parameter, the normals of a WrapSurface defined by an infinite Cylinder are always pointing outwards.

Modeling.name: qAttributeFilter
Modeling.description: Note: This query is used only for legacy unnamed attributes, which are still supported but no longer reccommended. See the Attributes module for details.

parameters.name: attributePattern
parameters.description:
Will only resolve to queries whose legacy unnamed attributes match the type (and possibly the values) of this pattern.
If attributePattern has a type tag, will only match attributes with that same type tag. 
EXAMPLE
{} as MyCustomType will match all attributes with type tag MyCustomTypeIf the attribute has no type tag (i.e. it is a standard type like string or map), will match all attributes with that same standard type. 
EXAMPLE
"asdf" will match all string attributes. EXAMPLE
{} will match all map attributes.If the attribute is a map, will only match maps which have identical values for every key-value pair in the pattern 
EXAMPLE
{ "odd" : true } matches all unnamed map attributes that have a field "odd" whose value is true. EXAMPLE
{ "odd" : true } as MyCustomType matches all unnamed map attributes with the that have a field "odd" whose value is true.

Modeling.name: qAttributeQuery

Math.name: approximateSpline
Math.description: Compute a family of splines that approximates a family of ApproximationTargets to within a given tolerance. The resulting splines are consistently parameterized, so that, for example, lofting between them will match corresponding target positions. Note: If parameters are not specified, the magnitude of start and end derivatives in targets is ignored as well as the second component parallel with the first derivative.

parameters.name: degree
parameters.description: The desired degree of the curve. The output may have a different degree, if for example there aren't enough points.

parameters.name: tolerance
parameters.description: How far the output is allowed to deviate from the input. Must be at least 1e-8 meters.

parameters.name: isPeriodic
parameters.description: Whether the output spline is periodic.

parameters.name: targets
parameters.description: An array of ApproximationTargets. All targets must have the same number of positions and specify corresponding derivative information.

parameters.name: parameters
parameters.description: OptionalAn array of numbers representing the parameters corresponding to the target points. Must be strictly increasing. If specified, the output spline at those parameters will match the target points. If specified, derivatives in approximation targets will not be rescaled.

parameters.name: maxControlPoints
parameters.description: OptionalThe maximum number of control points that will be returned by this function's output. Tolerance will not be satisfied if this limit is reached. Default is 10000.

parameters.name: interpolateIndices
parameters.description: OptionalAn array of indices into target positions that specifies which ones are to be interpolated exactly. This is currently supported only for non-periodic splines.

parameters.name: suppressInterpolationNotice
parameters.description: OptionalDon't report an info if the result is fully interpolated. Default is false.

parameters.name: array
parameters.type: An array of BSplineCurves, one for each target.

Math.name: bSplineSurface
Math.description: Returns a new BSplineSurface, adding knot padding and control point overlap as necessary.

parameters.name: uDegree
parameters.description: The degree of the spline in u.

parameters.name: vDegree
parameters.description: The degree of the spline in v.

parameters.name: isUPeriodic
parameters.description: Whether the spline periodic in u.

parameters.name: isVPeriodic
parameters.description: Whether the spline periodic in v.

parameters.name: controlPoints
parameters.description:
A matrix of control points. See BSplineSurface for specific detail. If u or v is periodic, you may provide the necessary overlap, or provide control points without any overlap. If no overlap is provided, degree overlapping control point rows or columns (corresponding to the first degree control point rows or columns) will be added. (unless you provide a set of knots that show no overlap is necessary). 
EXAMPLE
controlPointMatrix([
    [vector(-1, -1, -1) * inch, vector(-1, 0, 0) * inch, vector(-1, -2, 1) * inch],
    [vector( 0,  1, -1) * inch, vector( 0, 2, 0) * inch, vector( 0,  0, 1) * inch],
    [vector( 1, -1, -1) * inch, vector( 1, 0, 0) * inch, vector( 1, -2, 1) * inch]
])

parameters.name: weights
parameters.description: OptionalA matrix of weights. See BSplineSurface for specific detail.

parameters.name: uKnots
parameters.description: OptionalAn array of knots. See BSplineSurface for specific detail. If knots are not provided a uniform parameterization will be created such that the u parameterization exists on the range [0, 1]. For non-periodic u with n control point rows, you may provide the full set of n + degree + 1 knots, or you may provide n - degree + 1 knots, and multiplicity will by padded onto the ends (which has the effect of clamping the surface to the control points in the first and last rows). For periodic u with n unique control points (and optionally an additional degree overlapping control points), you may provide the full set of n + 2 * degree + 1 knots, or you may provide n + 1 knots, and the periodic knots will be padded onto the ends.

parameters.name: vKnots
parameters.description: OptionalSee uKnots.

parameters.description: OptionalA coordinate system representing the plane for the ImageMappingType.PLANAR type. This field must be defined if the imageMappingType field is of type ImageMappingType.PLANAR. The lower-left corner of the image will project to the plane's origin. The right edge of the image is along the positive X direction of the coordinate system. The top edge of the image is along the positive Y direction of the coordinate system. See planeToCSys for deriving a coordinate system from a Plane object.

parameters.name: cylinder
parameters.description: OptionalThe cylinder onto which the decal is mapped. This field must be defined if the imageMappingType field is of type ImageMappingType.CYLINDRICAL.

parameters.name: cylinderSystem
parameters.description: OptionalA coordinate system used in projecting the image onto the given cylinder. This field must be defined if the imageMappingType field is of type ImageMappingType.CYLINDRICAL. The coordinate system's origin must lie on the cylinder's axis with the system's Z axis aligned with the cylinder's own axis. The center of the horizontal extents of the image coincide with the intersection of the coordinate system's x axis and the cylinder. The center of the vertical extents of the image coincide with the projection of the coordinate system's origin on the cylinder. The top edge of the image is along the positive Z direction of the coordinate system projected on the cylinder.

If any profiles are collapsed, the names of the faces between the collapsed profiles are skipped. Supplying faceNames allows for the querying of faces by name when using qOpHoleFace.

Utilities.name: makeWrapSurface
Utilities.signature: (context is Context, face is Query, anchorPoint is Vector, spin is ValueWithUnits)
Utilities.description: Make a WrapSurface for opWrap defined by a planar, cylindrical or conical face.

parameters.name: face
parameters.description: A face to use as the definition face for the WrapSurface.

parameters.name: anchorPoint
parameters.description: The anchor point of the WrapSurface. See WrapSurface documentation.

parameters.name: spin
parameters.description:
For a planar face: Angle of a counter-clockwise spin to apply to the plane's x axis about its positive z axis, which is then used as the anchorDirection. For a cylindrical face: Angle of a counter-clockwise spin to apply to the cylinder's canonical anchorDirection at the given anchorPoint about the direction vector from the cylinder axis to the anchorPoint. The canonical anchorDirection at the given anchorPoint is defined as the "rightward" direction when looking at the cylinder in the direction from the anchorPoint to the cylinder axis with the cylinder's zAxis up. In other words: cross(cylinder z axis, direction vector from cylinder axis to anchorPoint). This spun direction is then used as the anchorDirection. For a conical face: Angle of a counter-clockwise spin to apply to the cone's canonical anchorDirection at the given anchorPoint about the normal at anchorPoint. The canonical anchorDirection at the given anchorPoint is defined as the "rightward" direction when looking at the cone from the normal.
See WrapSurface documentation for a description of anchorDirection.

Utilities.name: setDimensionedEntities
Utilities.description: Tolerant dimensions require multiple pieces of information. This function specifies all of the information required for a dimension that cannot be specified in a tolerant quantity. Tolerant quantities are commonly declared in a feature using the UIHint.CAN_BE_TOLERANT or UIHint.CAN_BE_TOLERANT_DIAMETER UI hints in the annotation of the quantity parameter.

parameters.name: parameterId
parameters.description: The id of the tolerant quantity parameter in the feature definition.

parameters.name: queries
parameters.description: An array of one query (for a radius or diameter dimension) or two queries (for other dimensions). The queries can evaluate to more than one face, but in that case each face should lie on the same underlying surface. See extrude and fillet for examples.

parameters.name: facePairs
parameters.description: Required if queries is undefinedAn array of pairs of queries (a pair is an array of two queries). Used for features where mulitple face pairs are subject to the same constraint but they are not all coincident, for example, a thin extrusion of a square where the thickness is tolerant.

parameters.name: measuresSolidAngle
parameters.description: OptionalUsed to specify which part of a circle an angle dimension refers to. The angle between two planes can be defined by two possible numbers that sum to 360 degrees. If this option is SOLID, then the angle is measured from the first face, in to the part. If this option is VOID, then the angle is measured from the first face, out of the part. If this option is not set for an angle, then the result is consistent but undefined. It is recommended that an option is always provided for angle dimensions.

parameters.name: measurementDirection
parameters.description: OptionalUsed with dimensions of type FeatureDimensionType.AXIS_DISTANCE. If this option is not set then the dimension measures the shortest distance between the axes. If this option is set then the dimension measures the distance between the axes in this direction.

parameters.name: schemaClass
parameters.description: OptionalOn regeneration a dimension with a quantity with tolerance type ToleranceType.DEFAULT will set its tolerances given the nominal value and any default tolerances specified on the part. If this field is not set then the rule used will be either the default linear or angular rule, depending on the dimension type. If this field is set then the dimension will use the custom rule corresponding to the value. This field can also be a ToleranceSchemaClass to use a predefined class from the standard library. For example, you can set this to ToleranceSchemaClass.FILLET_RADIUS to use the same tolerance rules as Onshape's official fillet feature.

parameters.name: tolerances
parameters.description: OptionalContains tolerance and precision information for the specified parameter. This cannot be set if the parameter has been marked tolerant by the user.

parameters.name: nominal
parameters.description: Required if tolerances is not undefinedRequired if setting tolerances, for either an existing or new parameter. For an existing feature parameter, this is usually the value of that parameter.

Onshape features.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, definition is map)
Onshape features.description: Feature performing an opDraft.

parameters.name: neutralPlane
parameters.description: Required if draftFeatureType is NEUTRAL_PLANE A planar face or mate connector defining both the neutral plane and pull direction of the the draft. The intersection of the drafted faces and the neutral plane remains unchanged. The pull direction of the draft will be the face normal or mate connector z-axis.

parameters.name: draftFaces
parameters.description: Required if draftFeatureType is NEUTRAL_PLANE The faces to draft for a NEUTRAL_PLANE draft.

parameters.name: pullDirectionEntity
parameters.description: Required if draftFeatureType is PARTING_LINE An entity defining the pull direction of the draft. This entity should conform to the ALLOWS_DIRECTION specification in QueryFilterCompound.

parameters.name: partingEdges
parameters.description: Required if draftFeatureType is PARTING_LINE Edges defining the parting line of the draft. These edges will remain unchanged as some adjacent faces, as defined by partingLineSides, are drafted.

parameters.name: hintFaces
parameters.description: OptionalFor Onshape internal use. For PARTING_LINE draft, specifies in advance which adjacent faces of partingEdges should be treated as more along the pull direction. When unspecified, the feature will use a geometric calculation to determine this distinction.

parameters.name: partingLineSides
parameters.description: Required if draftFeatureType is PARTING_LINE Specifies whether to draft one or both faces adjacent to the parting edges, and whether the draft should be symmetrical if drafting both faces. See PartingLineSides.

parameters.name: alongPull
parameters.description: Required if PartingLineSides is ONE_SIDED Specifies which face will be drafted in a ONE_SIDED PARTING_LINE draft. If true, the face which is more along the pull direction from the perspective of the parting edge is drafted. If false, the face which is more away from the pull direction from the perspective of the parting edge is drafted.

parameters.name: angle
parameters.description:
The draft angle, must be between 0 and 89.9 degrees. 
EXAMPLE
3 * degree

parameters.name: pullDirection
parameters.description: OptionalWhether the pull direction of the draft should be reversed. In equivalent terms, whether the draft should use -angle as the draft angle (true), or angle as the draft angle (false). Default is false.

parameters.name: secondAngle
parameters.description:
Required if PartingLineSides is TWO_SIDED The second draft angle for a TWO_SIDED PARTING_LINE draft. Must be between 0 and 89.9 degrees. Note that when using TWO_SIDED, angle will be applied to faces that are away from the pull direction, from the perspective of the edge. secondAngle will be applied to faces that are along the pull direction, from the perspective of the edge. 
EXAMPLE
3 * degree

parameters.name: secondPullDirection
parameters.description: OptionalWhether the pull direction of the draft should be reversed for the second angle of a TWO_SIDED draft. In equivalent terms, whether the draft should use -secondAngle as the second draft angle (true), or secondAngle as the second draft angle (false). Default is false.

parameters.name: tangentPropagation
parameters.description: OptionalFor a NEUTRAL_PLANE draft, true to propagate draft across tangent faces. Default is false.

parameters.name: referenceEdgePropagation
parameters.description: OptionalFor a PARTING_LINE draft, true to extend the parting line across connected edges of already included faces and tangent faces. Default is false.

parameters.name: reFillet
parameters.description: Optionaltrue to attempt to defillet draft faces before the draft and reapply the fillets after. Default is false.

enums.name: HolePositionReference
enums.description: For a HoleProfile, a reference point along the hole axis to which the position of the profile is relative. To calculate these references, the cylinder of the hole is intersected with the targets of the hole. If the hole cylinder encounters a slanted or otherwise irregular face at the intersection with the target, the reference may by a range rather than a single point. Users may specify that they want the end of this range by using a holeProfile, or the beginning of this range by using a holeProfileBeforeReference; or they may control this behavior directly by setting the beforeReference flag of the HoleProfile.

parameters.name: AXIS_POINT
parameters.type: When calling opHole, the user will supply one or more axes defining where the holes are to be placed. When using this reference, the position of the profile will be in reference to the origin of the axis Line of the hole.

parameters.name: TARGET_START
parameters.type: When using this reference, the position of the profile will be in reference to the closest intersection of the hole cylinder with any target.

parameters.name: LAST_TARGET_START
parameters.type: For each target, find the first intersection of the hole cylinder into the target. When using this reference, the position of the profile will be in reference to the furthest of those intersections. Notably, this means that if certain targets are geometrically constructed such that the hole cylinder enters and exits the target multiple times, only the first of the entrances into the target is considered.

parameters.name: LAST_TARGET_END
parameters.type: When using this reference, the position of the profile will be in reference to the furthest exit of the hole cylinder from any target.

parameters.name: LAST_TARGET_START_IN_DEPTH
parameters.type: For each target, find the first intersection of the hole cylinder into the target. When using this reference, the position of the profile will be in reference to the furthest of those intersections within the hole depth.

parameters.name: ALLOW_ARRAY_FOCUS

parameters.name: SHOW_INLINE_CONFIG_INPUTS

parameters.name: FOCUS_ON_VISIBLE
